subject: Private deployment: Pinning, maintenance window & circuit-breaker rollback proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sydney Park <sydney@acmehealth.com>, Ops Team <ops@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: Pinning, maintenance window & circuit-breaker rollback proposal

Hi Sydney / Acme ops team,

Following our runbook review last week, please find a proposed approach for the upcoming Private (VPC) patch wave on your environment. This note focuses on three areas we agreed to validate: version pinning semantics, maintenance window timing, and an automated circuit-breaker rollback ladder.

Short summary of the proposal (high level):
- Pin strategy: support short-term pin at the node-pool level (customer-controlled) + automatic soft-pin override after 72h for critical security fixes.
- Window: narrow 90-minute maintenance windows in rolling tranches across availability zones. Prefer local off-peak 02:00-03:30 in customer TZ; recommend Fridays to minimize business impact but open to Mon/Tues on request.
- Rollback ladder: three tiers — instant circuit-breaker (automated), staged reversal (canary -> slice rollback), and emergency full-shelve (manual). See attachments for diagrams.

Key asks for Acme Health before we lock schedule:
1) Confirm preferred maintenance window (local timezone and weekday).
2) Identify two on-call contacts for the weekend window (primary + backup).
3) Confirm appetite for our 72h soft-unpin policy for urgent security evictions.

I've attached a concise runbook, the PV evacuation diagram, and a canary test plan for the first tranche. The runbook includes abort criteria, token-level cost/latency checks, and end-to-end verification steps for the model runtime and KV cache integrity.

Notes on safety and observability:
- Circuit-breaker triggers: >5% 5-minute error rate delta OR median tail latency doubling vs baseline OR failed canary generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE drop > threshold).
- On trigger: automatic traffic re-route to pinned-safe model variant + alert to escalation channel.
- We will keep a 30-minute cooling window before starting staged reversal to collect telemetry.

Attachment stubs: upgrade-runbook-v1.2.pdf (20 pages), pv-evacuation-diagram.png, canary-test-plan.md

If this all looks good I will propose two candidate windows and circulate the final runbook for your legal/ops sign-off.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: Pinning, maintenance window & circuit-breaker rollback proposal

+1 to Karthik's plan. A couple of operational notes from the Dedicated/Private ops playbook that we should fold in before we finalize: 
- Preflight gating: run canary generation and KV cache snapshot 24h prior; if snapshot delta > 2% in token distribution, escalate to staging run.
- Network drains: coordinate with Acme's NetOps for BGP announcement damping during node cordon to avoid flapping. We should list the exact ASNs and point-of-contact in the final runbook.
- Restore timing: the staged reversal should be limited to two slices (20% each) with health checks at 10 and 30 minutes. If both fail, escalate to emergency shelve.

I'll add the NetOps contact template and the preflight checklist to the runbook and push version v1.3 once we get Sydney's window preference.

Monica
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood

Subject: Re: Private deployment: Pinning, maintenance window & circuit-breaker rollback proposal

Thanks Karthik & Monica — this reads well. A few questions from our side before we greenlight: 
1) For the 72h soft-unpin: if a security fix is auto-applied after 72h, what is the customer-facing notification SLA? We need at least 24h advance notice for any non-emergency changes.
2) Can you elaborate on how model-variant compatibility is guaranteed for automatic reroute? We run a quantized variant in our on-prem fleet; we need confirmation that the safe variant will not degrade inference output beyond our acceptance delta.
3) Regarding the two slices in staged reversal: can we reduce to 10% steps for the first tranche? We prefer more granular monitoring.

Also, our primary on-call is myself (mobile +1-415-555-0182); backup is Mark Chen (mark.chen@acmehealth.com). Preferred window is Saturday 02:00-03:30 PT (low traffic), but open if Redwood prefers Friday to align ops rotations.

Sydney
VP Engineering, Acme Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sydney Park <sydney@acmehealth.com>, Ops Team <ops@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 May 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: Pinning, maintenance window & circuit-breaker rollback proposal

Thanks — good questions, answered inline below.

1) 72h soft-unpin notification: we will treat the soft-unpin as a last-resort automatic policy for critical CVEs (CVSS >= 8.0) only. Notification SLA: 24h pre-notification when possible; for immediate critical-killchain fixes we will notify within 2 hours and follow up with a detailed incident record. We will add an opt-out flag for Acme if you want to retain manual-only approval for non-zero-day fixes.

2) Model-variant compatibility: the platform enforces a compatibility matrix at deployment time. For your quantized variant we will pin the logic to select a fallback variant that shares the same tokenizer and logits post-processing; we will run a narrow synthetic-quality canary (attached) that compares a sampled prompt set and rejects reroute if quality delta exceeds 3% of baseline. If the canary fails, automatic circuit-breaker will prefer traffic shed to a read-only fallback (serve cached responses) rather than a lower-quality model variant.

3) Slice size: we can accommodate 10% initial slices for the first tranche and then 20% for subsequent slices. That will add ~20 minutes to the overall window for monitoring, still within your 90-minute maximum. Monica's preflight checklist will enforce the additional monitoring hooks.

Next steps:
- I will update the runbook to v1.3 with the NetOps contact template, 10% slice option, and the explicit notification SLA language.
- Propose we lock Saturday 2025-06-14 02:00-03:30 PT as tranche 1 candidate; Karthik will send the formal invite and a short dry-run for telemetry collection a week prior.

If that works, I will also add a DocuSign link for the minimal maintenance approval (non-binding) so we have a record of the window and contacts.

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
